title.narrative: Strengthening resilience of vulnerable women and girls to cope with impact of GBV with the event of La Nina in Biadoa, Xudur and Afmadow

description.narrative: Women and adolescent girls suffer increased GBV risks in Somalia during catastrophic climatic and conflict events. Displacements, erosion of livelihoods and incomes, food insecurity are major factors that contribute to reduced capacities of women and girls to cope with humanitarian situation and ensure economic and physical security of themselves and their families. Women-headed households, divorced/widowed women, those living with disabilities and minority clans are the most impacted due the double disadvantage of age, loss of spouses, limited mobility, and clan discrimination. Most especially, women-headed households, widows, married and unmarried adolescents are particularly impacted by food insecurity often caused by drought situations. They often take on roles as primary or co-primary breadwinners for their families and may suffer exposure to sexual violence, abuse and exploitation and intimate partner violence as they seek to provide food and basic needs for their families. Anecdotal reports from focus group discussions of the GBV AoR partners and Joint multi-cluster assessments in South central regions of Somalia indicate that sexual exploitation is becoming more common, particularly for women working as domestic workers. The GBVIMS data 3rd quarter 2024 report indicate that the trend of intimate partner violence at 52% and rape at 13% compared 57% for IPV and 17%for Rape for the 3rd quarter report of 2023. During these drought situation, women and girls may not be able to maintain personal hygiene as a result depleted financial capacity. GBV/CP joint assessment reports in 2023 indicate increasing demand for dignity and menstrual hygiene kits by IDP women and girls. Drought incidence disrupts livelihoods/incomes, water and food supplies and compels families to seek opportunities for incomes and livelihoods elsewhere, thus resulting in creating displacements and resettling of women and girls to unfamiliar environments. This poses safety concerns and contributes to increasing the vulnerability of women and girls to GBV. It is important to strengthen the personal and collective resilience of women and girls to anticipate, cope and protect themselves from GBV incidences that may occur because of such situations. In view of the above, this project will target a total of 13,809 individuals, including 6,600 women, 4,620 girls, 965 men, and 1,624 boys. It will support initiatives designed to strengthen the resilience of women and girls and improve their capacity to cope with the increased occurrence of GBV prior to and during the period of La Niña drought. The project will ensure that GBV specialized services are available and accessible within the targeted locations. Additionally, it will support GBV prevention initiatives to enable women and girls to implement personal protective mechanisms against GBV.Project activities include preparatory activities which include procurement and prepositioning of dignity and reusable menstrual hygiene kits, identification and orientation for GBV case managers, Psycho-social and Clinical Management of Rape actors capacity in GBV stop centres and women and girls safe spaces in locations and proximity to target locations. The project will also support cash assistance through case management, service mapping, update and dissemination of referral pathways and community awareness and sensitization on how to prevent and cope with the occurrence of GBV during the drought event
